comments: Point-source approximation maintains interpretability while enabling gradient computation; FEM validation confirms mapping to physical labyrinthine geometries.

outputs: Optimized phase delays for metasurface array

hypotheses.hypothesis: Real loudspeaker response differs sufficiently from ideal source to alter optimal metasurface design
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: measured impulse response yields distinct phase delays compared to point-source model

title: Benchmarking mass-optimized noise absorbers
task: Benchmark and optimize broadband passive acoustic noise absorbers
key_results: Parallel design suits moderate bandwidth; series design superior for broad high-frequency absorption; porous cavity material beneficial at low frequencies via stiffness reduction
comments: Systematic comparison reveals limited improvement of complex designs over classical benchmarks; future progress requires mass-stiffness co-design.

model_io.model: Acoustic absorber with parallel/series layer configuration

hypotheses.hypothesis: Porous material in cavities enhances low-frequency absorption via stiffness reduction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: cavity stiffness reduction outweighs mass ineffectiveness at low frequencies

title: Electrospun fibers with axially polarized ferroelectric nematic core
task: Confine ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals in electrospun polymer fibers
key_results: Continuous FNLC core in hollow fiber preserved ferroelectric order; thin fibers (1 μm core) show uniform axial polarization; thick fibers exhibit twist along diameter
comments: Polarization stiffening counterintuitively suppresses Rayleigh-Plateau instability; twisted states warrant further investigation regarding ground-state nature.

model_io.model: Coaxial electrospun fiber with FNLC core

hypotheses.hypothesis: Polarization stiffening prevents fiber breakup via Rayleigh-Plateau instability
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: FNLC fibers stable; ferroelectric order preserved with polarization twist in thick fibers

title: Layer stacking order tunes thermal and mechanical properties in a prototypical imine-linked 2D covalent organic framework
task: Tune thermal and mechanical properties of 2D COF via layer stacking order
key_results: In-plane thermal conductivity k∥ ranges 1.02–1.14 W/m-K (ABC/AB-staggered); cross-plane k⊥ peaks at 0.14 W/m-K (AB-serrated); anisotropy k∥/k⊥ spans 5–16
comments: Molecular dynamics study demonstrates decoupled in-plane vs. cross-plane transport mechanisms; dipole-aligned linker modification modulates k∥ by 25% and k⊥ by 35%.

model_io.model: Molecular dynamics simulations of TAPB-DMPDA COF

hypotheses.hypothesis: Layer stacking order decouples in-plane and cross-plane thermal transport in 2D COFs
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: stacking geometry and interlayer spacing control thermal transport anisotropy independently

title: Metasurface-enabled OAM transmitters for high-capacity optical wireless links
task: Generate high-purity OAM beams at telecom wavelengths via metasurface-VCSEL integration
key_results: VCSEL + dielectric metasurface produces OAM beams at 1310 nm; dual-band operation (1310, 1550 nm) and broadband scalability demonstrated; precursor to integrated transmitters
comments: Non-monolithic proof-of-concept leverages VCSEL scalability and metasurface wavefront control; integration into single chip needed for practical deployment.

outputs: High-purity OAM beam (orbital angular momentum quantum number l)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Metasurface-shaped VCSEL output enables efficient OAM generation across telecom bands
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: high-purity OAM beams generated at 1310 and 1550 nm with broadband scalability

title: Toward multiband sensing in FR3: frequency anisotropy characterization and non-contiguous bands aggregation algorithms
task: Enable coherent multiband sensing in FR3 (7–24 GHz) for 6G ISAC
key_results: Characterized frequency anisotropy of sensing targets over GHz-wide bands; proposed phase coherence metrics for non-contiguous band aggregation; algorithm mitigates FR3 non-contiguity artifacts
comments: First experimental study of multiband ISAC in FR3; practical cm-level sensing resolution demonstrated but requires further validation across diverse target types.

inputs: Carrier phase from multiple non-contiguous FR3 bands

hypotheses.hypothesis: Frequency anisotropy of targets causes sensing errors in multiband aggregation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: new algorithm successfully mitigates artifacts from non-contiguous FR3 band configuration
